nodes.summary: Algorithms on numbers, polynomials and matrices: integer and polynomial multiplication (Karatsuba, FFT and convolution), matrix multiplication (iterative, recursive, Strassen), Horner evaluation, floating-point rounding, modular exponentiation and linear congruences, Miller-Rabin primality testing, and bit-level polynomial and bitvector arithmetic.
nodes.title: Algebraic and numerical algorithms

nodes.summary: Polynomial-time algorithms with proved approximation ratios for NP-hard optimization: vertex cover, set cover, metric TSP, list scheduling, maximum coverage.
nodes.title: Approximation algorithms

nodes.summary: Algorithms on points and segments in the plane: orientation and segment intersection, sweep-line intersection detection, convex hulls and closest pair; geometric search structures stay in Data structures.
nodes.title: Computational geometry

nodes.summary: Specific concurrent or distributed systems and their verified properties: deadlock and its detection, the banker's algorithm, dining philosophers, and communication protocols such as the alternating-bit protocol and go-back-N.
nodes.title: Concurrent systems and protocols

nodes.summary: Cryptographic schemes and their correctness and security reductions: public-key encryption and key agreement, signatures, identification protocols, pseudorandom functions, perfect secrecy and hash-function constructions including the birthday bound.
nodes.title: Cryptography

nodes.summary: Representations of collections with their invariants, operations and costs (worst-case and amortized), whether the structure is developed on its own or as an augmented variant; an algorithm that merely uses a structure goes to the field of the problem it solves.
nodes.title: Data structures

nodes.summary: Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normal forms and lossless decomposition, and transaction concurrency control (conflict serializability, two-phase locking).
nodes.title: Databases

nodes.summary: Optimization problems solved by tabulated recurrences: knapsack variants, subset sum, rod cutting, matrix-chain ordering, optimal binary search trees, longest common and longest increasing subsequences (including patience sorting) and maximum subarray (Kadane and divide-and-conquer); string edit distance goes to String algorithms.
nodes.title: Dynamic programming

nodes.summary: Algorithms computing properties of explicit graphs (traversal, connectivity, shortest paths, spanning trees, flows, matchings, Euler circuits) with correctness and cost proofs; pure graph theory belongs to GraphTheory, and verifiers or reductions for NP problems belong to TheoryOfComputation.
nodes.title: Graph algorithms

nodes.summary: Greedy choice and exchange arguments: the matroid greedy algorithm and its characterization of matroids, graphic matroids, interval scheduling and furthest-in-future offline caching.
nodes.title: Greedy algorithms and matroids

nodes.summary: Search and decision procedures from artificial intelligence: A* search, game-tree search with alpha-beta pruning, arc consistency for constraint satisfaction, and value and policy iteration for Markov decision processes.
nodes.title: Heuristic search and planning

nodes.summary: Mathematical theory of learning from data, including the probabilistic modelling, inference and sampling methods used in machine learning.
nodes.title: Machine learning

nodes.summary: Algorithms that act on a request sequence without knowing the future, and competitive-ratio upper and lower bounds: paging, list update, ski rental, online bipartite matching.
nodes.title: Online algorithms

nodes.summary: Work-span models, Brent's theorem and greedy scheduling, parallel prefix sums (Blelloch, Kogge-Stone) and pointer-jumping list ranking.
nodes.title: Parallel algorithms

nodes.summary: Algebraic models of concurrent processes: labelled transition systems and their runs, strong and weak bisimulation, observational congruence, CCS (choice, parallel composition, restriction, recursion, finite-state agents) and the pi-calculus.
nodes.title: Process calculi and behavioural equivalence

nodes.summary: Logics for proving programs correct: Hoare logic for partial and total correctness with soundness and relative completeness, weakest preconditions, verification-condition generation, and separation logic.
nodes.title: Program logics and verification

nodes.summary: Operational and denotational semantics of programming languages and correctness of compilation: the IMP language (syntax, big- and small-step, heap semantics, denotational semantics, stack-machine compilation), PCF with adequacy and contextual equivalence, CPS translation and closure conversion.
nodes.title: Programming language semantics

nodes.summary: Algorithms for quantum computers and their analysis: Grover search and the classical order-to-factor core of Shor's algorithm.
nodes.title: Quantum algorithms

nodes.summary: Algorithms whose identity is their use of randomness or whose analysis averages over random inputs: expected running time under input distributions, Fisher-Yates shuffling, the hiring problem, Karger's minimum cut, Freivalds' matrix-product check and MinHash similarity sketches.
nodes.title: Randomized algorithms and probabilistic analysis

nodes.summary: Comparison and distribution sorting algorithms (including their expected-cost analyses), and searching and selection in lists and arrays (binary and linear search, quickselect, median of medians, simultaneous min-max). Comparator sorting networks, their depth and the 0-1 principle form the Sorting networks subfield.
nodes.title: Sorting and searching

nodes.summary: Exact pattern matching (naive, finite automaton, Knuth-Morris-Pratt, Boyer-Moore, Rabin-Karp, Z algorithm) and edit distance with edit scripts; biological sequence alignment belongs to Biology.
nodes.title: String algorithms

nodes.summary: Typed lambda calculi and type inference: the simply typed lambda calculus (syntax, substitution, normalization, logical relations, normalization by evaluation, elaboration, its models), lambda calculus with references and type safety, and Hindley-Milner let-polymorphism with Algorithm W.
nodes.title: Type systems and lambda calculi

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
